rationale: This mixed-methods study in Koja, Jakarta combines a resident survey (analyzed via exploratory factor analysis, cluster analysis, and logistic regression) with semi-structured stakeholder interviews and field observations to examine community-based urban sanitation programs. The central programmatic mechanism analyzed is community collaboration, socialization, educational outreach, and participatory facility management (participation_assistance), alongside a secondary sanitation-governance factor capturing regular regulatory monitoring and oversight (enforcement_sanctions). Across all eight hypotheses (H1-H8) and the logistic regression model, the focal empirical dependent variable is citizen willingness to participate in community-based sanitation programs (alongside attitudinal clusters), which represents an institutional/governance intermediate outcome (administrative_outcome) rather than direct household hookup or service quality metrics.
